title: Dynamic Reducers
definition: The architectural pattern of injecting new reducers into the Redux store AFTER the application has already started running, rather than defining all reducers upfront in `configureStore`.
simpleExplanation: If you have a massive app with 50 features, loading all 50 Reducers on the initial page load will make your website incredibly slow. Dynamic reducers allow you to load the 'Checkout' reducer ONLY when the user actually navigates to the Checkout page.
realWorldExample: A Micro-frontend architecture. The core shell app loads. When the user clicks the 'Support Chat' widget, the browser downloads the Chat JavaScript, and dynamically injects the `chatReducer` into the running Redux store.

basic: What Redux store method is used to swap out or inject reducers at runtime?
intermediate: If a dynamically injected slice dispatches an action BEFORE it is injected, what happens?

answers.question: Dispatched before injection?
answers.answer: The action will fire, but because the specific reducer hasn't been injected yet, the action will hit the `default` switch cases of the existing reducers and do absolutely nothing. The data will be lost.

terminalOutput:
/*
  Conceptual flow of Code Splitting Reducers:

  1. App starts. configureStore() runs with ONLY the core reducers (auth, ui).
  2. User clicks 'Dashboard'.
  3. React Lazy loads the Dashboard.jsx component.
  4. Inside Dashboard.jsx, a useEffect runs:
     `store.injectReducer('dashboard', dashboardSlice.reducer)`
  5. The Redux store recalculates its state tree.
  6. The Dashboard component can now use `useSelector(state => state.dashboard)`.
*/
